cards.headline: Single-vehicle crash on Donald Ross Road in Jupiter kills one Sunday morning
cards.body:
A single-vehicle crash on Donald Ross Road in Jupiter Sunday morning killed one person, according to Jupiter police officials. The crash happened just before 6 a.m. when the driver came over railroad tracks, lost control of the vehicle, and struck a tree.

Police confirmed one adult male died in the crash but are withholding the victim's name pending notification of next of kin. The crash occurred on Donald Ross Road between Military Trail and Alternate A1A.

Both eastbound and westbound lanes of Donald Ross Road between Military Trail and Alternate A1A were closed for several hours as crash investigators worked the scene. The roadway has since reopened to traffic.

The Jupiter Police Department is continuing to investigate the circumstances that led to the fatal crash. The preliminary information came from officials at the scene Sunday morning.

cards.headline: Five competitive Florida House seats remain unchallenged days before qualifying deadline
cards.body:
With less than a week until the qualifying deadline on June 12, twenty-five Florida House district races have no challenger from one of the two major political parties. While most of these uncontested seats are in strongly partisan districts where a challenge would be unlikely to succeed, five races stand out as genuinely competitive. These five districts, which include two Republican-held seats and three Democratic-held seats, have voter margins narrow enough that the lack of opposition from the other party raises serious questions about campaign strategy and resource allocation.

The five competitive uncontested districts are scattered across Florida. House District 12 in Jacksonville, which favored Trump by 10 points in 2024, has only Republican Terrance Freeman running to succeed term-limited Representative Wyman Duggan. House District 44 in Orange County is a solidly Democratic district where Rita Harris is running unopposed for her third term, having won reelection in 2024 with 65 percent of the vote. House District 60 in Pinellas County covers parts of St. Petersburg and Pinellas Park and leans Democratic by 7 points. After incumbent Lindsay Cross announced her retirement, lawyer Lindsay Polega-Quigley filed to run and currently faces no opposition. House District 89 in Palm Beach County represents the closest race, with a Democratic lean of just 1 point. Democratic Representative Debra Tendrich won the seat in 2024 by only 2 points and is running unopposed. House District 87 in Jupiter, which Democrat Emily Gregory flipped in a March upset, remains an important race as both parties assess their November prospects.

The Florida Democratic Party responded to questions about the unchallenged races by emphasizing their investment in year-round organizing and candidate recruitment. The party said over 1,300 Democrats have expressed interest in running over the past eighteen months. Republican Party of Florida Chair Evan Power expressed confidence that his party would expand its legislative supermajority, stating that "Floridians have rejected the radical left agenda" and that the Republican Party would "field quality candidates across Florida that will drive us to big victories."

Analysis by Matt Isbell of MCI Maps, based on 2024 presidential voting data, shows these competitive districts have voter divisions that suggest both parties could potentially mount successful campaigns. The August 18 primary election will be followed by the November general election. The qualifying deadline is June 12.

cards.headline: Indiantown brush fire grows to 125 acres over weekend, now 99% contained
cards.teaser: A brush fire that began Friday in Indiantown escalated over the weekend before being brought under near-total control, according to Martin County Fire Rescue an.
cards.body:
A brush fire that began Friday in Indiantown escalated over the weekend before being brought under near-total control, according to Martin County Fire Rescue and the Florida Forest Service. The incident started on Friday, June 5, when firefighters responded to a rapidly developing brush fire in the 2600 block of Southwest Warfield Boulevard just before 3:30 p.m. Crews quickly contained the blaze at approximately 37.8 acres, with no reported injuries and no structures threatened. The Florida Forest Service assisted by establishing plow lines to help stop the spread of flames, while Martin County Fire Rescue's drone team identified remaining hotspots and confirmed full containment before crews cleared the area.

By Saturday, June 6, the situation escalated significantly when crews returned to the same general area to battle a much larger 120-acre brush fire. Officials believe the fire rekindled from the previous day's incident, with shifting winds and dense vegetation contributing to rapid fire growth. The response included Martin County Fire Rescue, the Florida Forest Service, and the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Firefighters worked to protect nearby structures as smoke spread across the area, though officials confirmed there was no broader threat to the public. The fire had reached approximately 125 acres in total size and is 99% contained as of Sunday morning. Officials noted early indications suggested the fire may have been a holdover fire, with a lightning strike potentially smoldering underground before igniting visible flames. The Florida Forest Service continues to investigate the fire's origin.

cards.body:
Orion Jean Baptiste, a 9-year-old from Port St. Lucie, launched a new juniors chess club after developing a passion for the game at age 5 while playing with family. "I just wanted kids to learn about chess," Baptiste said, adding that he hopes "more people have respect for board games." The Atlantis Chess Club now meets every Friday at the Port St. Lucie City Center, where more than 36 juniors have already joined.

Diana Cowan Kempton, the club's program director, said the program aims to develop the next generation of leaders. "[It] will help to build leaders or members that are more focused, more patient, more strategic and thoughtful in their decision [making]," Kempton said. The club attracts players of all skill levels, including newcomers like Francesca Furlong, who said the best part is "playing with other kids." The club will soon expand with two additional programs at the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Transpire Help fundraiser draws LGBTQ+ community to West Palm Beach celebration
cards.teaser: Pride on the Block filled The Peach in West Palm Beach Saturday as the largest fundraiser for Transpire Help, a non-profit providing services to LGBTQ+ individuals.
cards.body:
The Peach in West Palm Beach hosted Pride on the Block on Saturday, the largest fundraiser for Transpire Help, a non-profit organization providing substance use treatment, mental health care, and stable housing to LGBTQ+ individuals. Donna Weinberger, founder of Transpire Help, said the event creates a space where attendees can feel celebrated and safe. "People can come and be filled with unity and joy and happiness and be able to be in one spot and feel safe," Weinberger said.

For performer Liam Chambers, the event held deep personal meaning. Chambers credits Transpire Help with helping turn his life around, saying he is three years sober and now performs as a drag king, which he would not have been able to do without the organization. Weinberger emphasized that a significant portion of the community, especially gender diverse individuals, lack health insurance or funds to access treatment. The fundraiser has become increasingly critical as cuts to government funding have slashed the number of people the organization can help in half. Jack Cesivon, an LGBTQ+ community member, said Transpire has helped people that literally have nobody.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County parents respond to teen takeover at Wellington mall
cards.teaser: A social media post promoting a teen takeover at the Wellington Green Mall gained nearly 100,000 views, prompting an increased Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office presence.
cards.body:
A social media post promoting a teen takeover at Wellington Green Mall gained nearly 100,000 views, prompting the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office to deploy an increased law enforcement presence. Shoppers at the mall on Friday noticed the heightened police activity. Savanna Restrepo, who was picking up her son Isaac from summer camp, said she had seen posts circulating online about the event beforehand. She said the visible police presence was reassuring and indicated that authorities were aware of what was happening in the community and taking a proactive approach.

Teen takeovers are large gatherings of teens at malls, beaches or parks that typically devolve into violence. The trend has spread across Florida, including an event in Clearwater at the end of May that resulted in widespread property damage, fights and the shooting of a 17-year-old. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier called the events "unacceptable" on social media and announced a plan to "investigate and prosecute those who are responsible for these events." Palm Beach County Commissioner Greg Weiss said community safety is a priority but noted that kids need structured activities. He pointed out that Palm Beach County offers scholarship opportunities for summer camps and emphasized that parental involvement is essential, urging parents to know what their children are doing.

cards.headline: Florida dive operators fight federal shark feeding ban proposal
cards.teaser: A federal proposal to ban shark feeding off Florida's coast is drawing sharp criticism from the state's shark diving industry, which warns the measure could devastate conservation-driven tourism businesses.
cards.body:
The Safe Florida Seas Act, H.R. 3831, cleared the U.S. House and would prohibit shark feeding in federal waters within 200 miles of Florida, with an exception for harvesting. Supporters call it a common-sense safety measure to reduce human-shark interactions. However, a coalition of dive operators argues the bill unfairly targets their work, which includes veteran-owned small businesses and nonprofits focused on education and conservation, while leaving fishing practices untouched. Nathan Campbell, owner of Emerald Charters, says Congress has not asked dive operators to present data or explain their practices.

Operators distinguish their methods from commercial fishing, saying they avoid surface chumming and instead take bait underwater during dives. This approach, they argue, is less likely to condition sharks to approach boats for food, unlike some harvesting operations that release hundreds of gallons of chum at the surface. Dr. Matt Ajemian, an associate research professor at Florida Atlantic University, says shark diving in Florida has a near perfect safety record. Campbell points to Hawaii's 2006 ban on baited shark diving as a cautionary tale, noting that shark incidents have increased there since the ban and that at least one in four fishing trips ends with a shark biting off part of the catch, according to the Western Pacific Regional Fishery Management Council. Campbell is urging senators to delay action, gather research, and involve all stakeholders in shaping new rules.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County rental assistance applications close quickly amid high demand
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County's Emergency Rental Assistance Program receives about 600 applications in the first couple of hours they open each month, with nearly 8,000 calls for housing assistance monthly.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County's Community Services Department has nearly $2 million in combined grant funding for its Emergency Rental Assistance Program, designed to help residents who can't pay rent. However, demand far outweighs available funds each month. Program director Dr. James Green told WPTV that the county typically receives about 600 applications within the first couple of hours applications open, and receives nearly 8,000 calls for housing assistance per month combined with 211. The county currently has about 800 applications in the queue for rental assistance. At the time of reporting, the county's assistance portal was marked closed due to high demand. Green urges anyone in need to call 1-833-CSD-WILL to check for availability.

According to the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the average rent for a one-bedroom in Palm Beach County is $2,020 a month. Green said the recent surge in applications is partly due to rising costs of living including housing, gas, and food. For those who cannot access the county's program, 211 is another option available 24/7 that connects residents with nonprofits and other assistance programs in the area. Green is calling on people with extra housing to partner with the county to help neighbors in need.

cards.headline: Florida voters divided on November property tax proposal
cards.teaser: Florida voters will decide this November whether to roll back property taxes by raising the homestead exemption for homeowners, a proposal drawing mixed reactions from West Palm Beach residents.
cards.body:
Florida voters will decide this November whether to raise the homestead exemption to roll back property taxes, a proposal drawing mixed reactions from West Palm Beach residents. The ballot measure would need 60% approval to pass. A similar proposal to raise the homestead exemption failed in 2018.

Brian Edington supports the idea because it benefits people who permanently live in Florida and saves homeowners. He said he is comfortable with local governments spending less, pointing to his own neighborhood's trash services as an example where cuts could be made. "I have trash services in my neighborhood, they pick it up twice, I don't need it twice a week, once a week would be adequate," Edington said. Rosabella Olivares expressed concern about reduced funding. "There's going to be less money because everything is expensive now," Olivares said. While homeowners were generally supportive of paying less in taxes, renters expressed more skepticism. One resident along Clematis Avenue in downtown West Palm Beach said the savings would not reach renters and predicted landlords would raise rent. A resident identified only as Stan said he does not think funding should be eliminated entirely because "infrastructure and all that stuff is important."

A social media post promoting a teen takeover at Wellington Green Mall gained nearly 100,000 views, prompting the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office to increase law enforcement presence at the mall on Friday. Teen takeovers are large gatherings of teens at malls, beaches or parks that typically devolve into violence. The trend has been spreading across Florida, including an event in Clearwater at the end of May that resulted in widespread property damage, fights and the shooting of a 17-year-old. Shoppers at the Wellington Green Mall noticed the heightened police presence. Savanna Restrepo, who was picking up her son Isaac from summer camp, said she had seen posts on different social media accounts about the event. She said the visible police presence was reassuring and lets residents know that officials are aware of what's going on in the community and want to take a proactive approach. Fellow parent Eric Delgado said the response was the right call and a strong police presence is needed.

With school out and teens having more time on their hands, Weiss said parents should be taking steps to fill that time through community rec centers that offer programming throughout the day. Weiss acknowledged that summer camp costs can be a barrier for some families and noted that Palm Beach County does offer scholarship opportunities for summer camps.

cards.headline: Summer fertilizer ban begins June 1 in Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties
cards.body:
Starting June 1, Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties are implementing a ban on fertilizers containing phosphorus or nitrogen. The restriction applies to anyone treating lawns or landscaping in these three counties through September 30.

According to Jordan Skaggs with Environmental Resources in St. Lucie County, the ban targets nutrient-rich runoff during the rainy season that can cause algae blooms in waterways like the Indian River Lagoon and St. Lucie River. "It can shade out beneficial plants to fish and wildlife," Skaggs said. "At certain densities, harmful algae blooms can release toxins that can affect human health, wildlife health and overall ecosystem health." Grantly Ricketts, director of University of Florida's Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences St. Lucie County Extension, recommends composting as an alternative during the ban. "It can be like a small trash can," Ricketts said. "That is the easiest and most practical way or means to add nutrients to your landscape."

hero.body:
Orion Jean Baptiste, a 9-year-old Port St. Lucie resident, has started a new junior chess club to encourage other young people to embrace the game. Baptiste first developed his interest in chess at age 5 while playing with family members, and he now wants to share that passion with his community. His goal is straightforward: to help kids learn chess and develop a greater appreciation for board games. The Atlantis Chess Club meets every Friday at Morningside Branch Library, where more than 36 junior members have already signed up. The club will soon expand with two additional programs launching at the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce.

Baptiste expressed concern about young people's focus on technology at the expense of traditional games. "Everybody's more focused on like tech stuff," he said. "I'm hoping that more people have respect for board games." Diana Cowan Kempton, the club's program director, sees chess as a valuable tool for developing young leaders. According to Kempton, the game will help build members who are more focused, patient, strategic, and thoughtful when making decisions. The club welcomes players of all experience levels, from complete beginners to those already skilled at the game who want to continue improving.

The club has attracted families seeking educational opportunities for their children. Thomas Furlong brought his two children to join, viewing it as an ideal setting where his daughter could learn the game and his son could advance his skills. He also appreciated the friendly competition between siblings. His daughter, Francesca Furlong, is one of the club's newest members and particularly enjoys the social aspect of playing with other children her age.

The Friday meetings at Morningside Branch Library remain open to any junior players from Port St. Lucie and surrounding areas of the Treasure Coast. Baptiste's initiative demonstrates how one young person's enthusiasm can create opportunities for many others in the community to explore a classic game that develops critical thinking skills and strategic planning abilities. The expanding program shows strong community support for chess instruction among young people in the region.

hero.headline: Beetlejuice musical runs through June 7 at Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
hero.teaser: The Broadway hit brings spooky humor and over-the-top visuals to the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall, with actor Ryan Stajmiger in the iconic striped suit.
hero.body:
Beetlejuice the musical is playing at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach, running June 2 through June 7. The Broadway hit brings its spooky humor, over-the-top visuals, and heartwarming moments to the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall. Actor Ryan Stajmiger steps into the iconic striped suit to play the mischievous demon beloved from Tim Burton's 1988 film.

The musical follows Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teen, whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a demon with a flair for trouble. Stajmiger says one of his favorite parts is laughing with the audience. He gets to break the fourth wall and communicate directly with the audience. Early in the run, he experienced an unexpected moment when his wig change went wrong and he was bald for an entire scene.

Performances include 7:30 p.m. shows on June 3 and June 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, matinee and evening performances on June 6, and a closing matinee on June 7. Tickets start at $34.50 and can be purchased at kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up, with parental discretion advised.

cards.headline: Over 100 paddlers to cross 80 miles of ocean from Bahamas to Lake Worth Beach for cystic fibrosis fundraiser
cards.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the Atlantic Ocean this June in the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis, launching from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13 and arriving at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. Event founder Travis Suit established the endurance trek to benefit the Piper's Angels Foundation, which he created in honor of his daughter, Piper, who was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4. The four-day event begins June 10 with participant arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove, followed by a 4Ocean beach cleanup and community buffet dinner on Thursday. Friday features a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony to honor cystic fibrosis warriors, with mandatory rest and safety checks before the overnight launch.

Safety requirements include U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation devices, waterproof whistles, and reflective gear during dark hours. All paddlers must wear GPS trackers provided by the event and remain active throughout the journey, with mandatory safety meetings required before departure. Paddlers must raise a minimum of $2,000, while crew and virtual participants must collect at least $500, with contributions due by July 31. Suit, an experienced paddler, created the event after learning about respiratory benefits of ocean salt air for people with cystic fibrosis. Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 for a daylong celebration welcoming the arriving paddlers.

hero.headline: Five competitive Florida House seats remain unchallenged days before qualifying deadline
hero.body:
With less than a week until the qualifying deadline on June 12, twenty-five Florida House district races have no challenger from one of the two major political parties. While most of these uncontested seats are in strongly partisan districts where a challenge would be unlikely to succeed, five races stand out as genuinely competitive. These five districts, which include two Republican-held seats and three Democratic-held seats, have voter margins narrow enough that the lack of opposition from the other party raises serious questions about campaign strategy and resource allocation.

The five competitive uncontested districts are scattered across Florida. House District 12 in Jacksonville, which favored Trump by 10 points in 2024, has only Republican Terrance Freeman running to succeed term-limited Representative Wyman Duggan. House District 44 in Orange County is a solidly Democratic district where Rita Harris is running unopposed for her third term, having won reelection in 2024 with 65 percent of the vote. House District 60 in Pinellas County covers parts of St. Petersburg and Pinellas Park and leans Democratic by 7 points. After incumbent Lindsay Cross announced her retirement, lawyer Lindsay Polega-Quigley filed to run and currently faces no opposition. House District 89 in Palm Beach County represents the closest race, with a Democratic lean of just 1 point. Democratic Representative Debra Tendrich won the seat in 2024 by only 2 points and is running unopposed. House District 87 in Jupiter, which Democrat Emily Gregory flipped in a March upset, remains an important race as both parties assess their November prospects.

The Florida Democratic Party responded to questions about the unchallenged races by emphasizing their investment in year-round organizing and candidate recruitment. The party said over 1,300 Democrats have expressed interest in running over the past eighteen months. Republican Party of Florida Chair Evan Power expressed confidence that his party would expand its legislative supermajority, stating that "Floridians have rejected the radical left agenda" and that the Republican Party would "field quality candidates across Florida that will drive us to big victories."

Analysis by Matt Isbell of MCI Maps, based on 2024 presidential voting data, shows these competitive districts have voter divisions that suggest both parties could potentially mount successful campaigns. The August 18 primary election will be followed by the November general election. The qualifying deadline is June 12.

cards.headline: Jay Collins to unveil senior protection initiative at Monday news conference
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate Jay Collins will hold a news conference Monday morning to introduce his Live Florida initiative aimed at making life more affordable for Florida seniors.
cards.body:
Jay Collins will hold a news conference Monday at 10 a.m. at McCall's Tavern on Alverez Ave. to unveil his "Live Florida" initiative as part of his gubernatorial campaign. The initiative aims to help seniors across Florida stay financially secure and independent as they age. Collins plans to address the main challenges facing the state's growing senior population, including rising costs for housing, insurance, healthcare, and other daily expenses. He will discuss his ideas for reducing fraud and cybersecurity threats that target retirees while boosting consumer protections and public safety.

Collins has previously worked on senior protection efforts. In November, he helped start Operation Senior Shield, a program designed to help seniors avoid scams in Florida. At a launch event in Jacksonville last year, Collins said the program "provides timely text and email alerts, so older adults and caregivers can stay ahead of scammers." As Republican lieutenant governor under Ron DeSantis, Collins is competing in the GOP Primary Election on August 18 against U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, the current front-runner. During an appearance on "Sunday Morning Futures" on Fox News, Collins criticized Donalds for being unwilling to debate, saying candidates must "stand up and show up" rather than "hide in the shadows."

cards.headline: Oliver Gilbert launches congressional campaign for CD 24, setting up Miami Gardens showdown
cards.teaser: Miami-Dade Commissioner Oliver Gilbert III will formally launch his campaign for Florida's 24th Congressional District on Sunday at Antioch Missionary Baptist Church in Miami Gardens.
cards.body:
Miami-Dade Commissioner Oliver Gilbert III will formally launch his campaign for Florida's 24th Congressional District on Sunday at 10 a.m. at Antioch Missionary Baptist Church in Miami Gardens, the city where he was born, raised, and twice elected Mayor. Gilbert resigned his county seat effective Jan. 3, filed his Statement of Candidacy with the Federal Election Commission, and launched a campaign site this past week. A Florida A&M University graduate with a law degree from the University of Miami, Gilbert, 53, led Miami Gardens as Mayor from 2012 to 2020 before winning a Miami-Dade Commission seat in District 1, where he served as Commission Chair from 2022 to 2024.

U.S. Rep. Frederica Wilson, 83, announced she would not seek a ninth term after eight terms in Congress. Wilson told the Miami Herald she deliberately held the news until Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new congressional map, fearing an earlier exit would turn the district into a redistricting target. The redraw kept CD 24 deeply blue, one of just four Democratic-leaning seats left in the state, which means the Aug. 18 Democratic Primary will effectively decide Wilson's successor. Gilbert enters a fast-forming field that includes former Miami-Dade Commissioner Jean Monestime, physician Rudy Moise, and business owner Christine Sanon-Jules, along with Republican Patricia Gonzalez and independent Andy Daro. State Sen. Shevrin Jones, 42, a fellow Miami Gardens Democrat and 14-year legislative veteran, is preliminarily viewed as the early front-runner. The qualifying deadline is June 12.

cards.headline: Germans increasingly view Florida as retirement hedge amid economic uncertainty
cards.teaser: Germany recently became the top foreign country searching for South Florida real estate online, according to the Miami Association of Realtors, signaling a shift in European retirement planning.
cards.body:
According to the Miami Association of Realtors, Germany recently became the No. 1 foreign country searching for South Florida real estate online. This reflects a quiet trend emerging across Florida's real estate market, where more Germans view the state not merely as a vacation destination but as a retirement plan. Many Germans are not making a dramatic move across the Atlantic but are easing into it over years, sometimes decades. One German homeowner has owned property in Florida for 16 years and today spends roughly half the year in the Sunshine State and half in Germany. He eventually obtained a Green Card, allowing him to spend far more time in Florida than most European visitors can.

German buyers arrive with specific expectations and are often surprised by how uncomplicated buying property in the United States can be, according to a Florida-based real estate professional who works extensively with German clients. Foreigners can buy homes without major restrictions, the paperwork is comprehensible, and the process moves quickly. One agent noted that German clients "want things organized. They want to know exactly how everything works," adding that there are more German buyers every year, not just in Cape Coral anymore. International buyers bring capital, support local businesses, hire property managers, contractors, landscapers, pool-service companies and real estate agents, contributing to the tax base while adding pressure to housing markets already struggling with affordability.

cards.headline: Navy veteran Dan Green enters CD 9 congressional race with $1 million investment
cards.teaser: Dan Green, a Navy reserve officer and Pentagon appointee under President Donald Trump, announced a campaign for Florida's 9th Congressional District with $1 million of his own money.
cards.body:
Dan Green, a Navy reserve officer and Pentagon appointee under President Donald Trump, announced a campaign for Florida's 9th Congressional District as the state's congressional qualifying week opened. The Vero Beach Republican said he is putting $1 million of his own money into the race and arrives with the backing of the War Veterans Fund, the group he co-founded in 2018 to elect veterans to Congress.

CD 9 changed dramatically through redistricting. Under the old lines it was an Osceola-anchored, Hispanic-majority district that Darren Soto had held comfortably since 2017, and one Kamala Harris carried with about 51% in 2024. Ron DeSantis's new map stretched it south through the middle of the peninsula and east to absorb all of Indian River County, Green's home turf. Florida Politics analysis found Trump would have won the redrawn seat with more than 58%. Green joins a Republican primary that already includes retired Marine and former F-18 pilot Justin Story, who has qualified by petition, and 2024 nominee Thomas Chalifoux. Green spent 23 years in the Navy, mobilized for tours in Afghanistan and Iraq, and was appointed Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Strategy and Force Development in 2019. His campaign says he carries endorsements from more than half a dozen congressional war veterans.

cards.body:

The crash happened just before 6 a.m. when the driver came over railroad tracks, lost control of the vehicle, and struck a tree. Police confirmed one adult male died in the crash but are withholding the victim's name pending notification of next of kin.

Both eastbound and westbound lanes of Donald Ross Road between Military Trail and Alternate A1A were closed for several hours as crash investigators worked the scene. The roadway has since reopened to traffic. The Jupiter Police Department is continuing to investigate the circumstances that led to the fatal crash.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie 9-year-old launches junior chess club to share love of the game
cards.teaser: A new juniors chess club has launched in Port St.
cards.body:
A new juniors chess club has launched in Port St. Lucie, inspired by 9-year-old Orion Jean Baptiste, who wanted to share his love of the game with his community. Baptiste's passion for chess began at age 5, playing alongside family. "I just wanted kids to learn about chess," Baptiste said. "Everybody's more focused on like tech stuff. I'm hoping that more people have respect for board games."

More than 36 juniors have already joined the Atlantis Chess Club, which meets at the Port St. Lucie library every Friday. Diana Cowan Kempton, the club's program director, said she hopes chess will help develop the next generation. "It will help to build leaders or members that are more focused, more patient, more strategic and thoughtful in their decision making," Kempton said. The club is attracting players of all skill levels. Thomas Furlong brought his children to the club, saying the setting is ideal for his family. "This is like the perfect chance for her to learn chess, my son to get better at chess and then them to have a little sibling rivalry competition," Furlong said. For Francesca Furlong, one of the club's newest members, the best part is playing with other kids. The club will soon begin two more programs at the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie 9-year-old launches junior chess club at community library
hero.body:
A 9-year-old Port St. Lucie boy has started a junior chess club to introduce his community to the game he loves. Orion Jean Baptiste began playing chess at age 5 with his family members and now wants to share that passion with other young people in the area. "I just wanted kids to learn about chess," Baptiste said. He believes chess deserves more respect in a world focused on technology. "Everybody's more focused on like tech stuff," Baptiste said. "I'm hoping that more people have respect for board games."

Diana Cowan Kempton, the club's program director, supports Baptiste's vision for what chess can accomplish. She believes the game will help build the next generation of thoughtful leaders. "It will help to build leaders or members that are more focused, more patient, more strategic and thoughtful in their decision making," Kempton said. The Atlantis Chess Club meets every Friday at the Port St. Lucie library and welcomes players at all skill levels, from beginners to experienced competitors.

The club has already grown to more than 36 junior members since its launch. Families like the Furlongs have been drawn to the program as a structured summer activity where children can learn together. Thomas Furlong brought his children to participate, seeing it as an opportunity for both his daughter to learn chess and his son to improve his skills. "This is like the perfect chance for her to learn chess, my son to get better at chess and then them to have a little sibling rivalry competition," Furlong said. For Francesca Furlong, one of the newest members, the appeal is straightforward. "I like playing with other kids," she said.

The club's success at the Port St. Lucie library has led to expansion plans. The Atlantis Chess Club will soon launch two additional programs at the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce, bringing chess opportunities to even more young people in the area. Through these efforts, Baptiste is achieving his goal of helping children appreciate board games while developing important skills like focus, patience and strategic thinking.

cards.headline: Pride on the Block fundraiser supports Transpire Help services in West Palm Beach

cards.body:
Pride on the Block brought together the LGBTQ+ community and supporters at The Peach in West Palm Beach Saturday as the largest fundraiser for Transpire Help, a non-profit organization that provides substance use treatment, mental health care, and stable housing to LGBTQ+ individuals. Donna Weinberger, founder of Transpire Help, said the event creates a space where attendees can feel celebrated and safe. Community members highlighted the event's importance, with one attendee noting the experience of being "amongst people who hear me and see me."

For performer Liam Chambers, the event held deep personal significance. Chambers credits Transpire Help with helping turn his life around, saying he is three years sober and now performs as a drag king thanks to the organization's support. Weinberger emphasized that the fundraiser is more important than ever, as cuts to government funding have slashed the number of people the organization can help in half. She noted that a significant portion of the LGBTQ+ community, particularly gender diverse individuals, do not have health insurance or funds to access treatment independently.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Sheriff increases presence at Wellington Green Mall after teen takeover posts
cards.teaser: A social media post promoting a teen takeover at Wellington Green Mall gained nearly 100,000 views, prompting increased law enforcement presence.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office increased law enforcement presence at Wellington Green Mall after a social media post promoting a teen takeover gained nearly 100,000 views. Shoppers at the mall on Friday noticed the heightened police presence. Savanna Restrepo, who was picking up her son Isaac from summer camp, said she had seen posts circulating online about the event and found the visible police response reassuring. "It just makes it feel safer," Restrepo said. "It lets us know that they're aware of what's going on in the community and they want to take that proactive approach." Fellow parent Eric Delgado also supported the response, saying "We need a strong police presence."

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier called the teen takeover events "unacceptable" and announced a plan to "investigate and prosecute those who are responsible for these events." Palm Beach County Commissioner Greg Weiss said community safety is a priority but pointed to a root cause of the trend. Weiss noted that kids need something to do during summer break and encouraged parents to utilize community recreation centers that offer programming throughout the day. The county offers scholarship opportunities for summer camps to help families with costs. Weiss emphasized the importance of parental involvement, urging parents to know what their children are doing and stay in contact with them.
